introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics, Paper 3 (0765/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown: A particle is projected from a point $O$ with speed $52\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\theta = \dfrac{5}{12}$. Find,
incertitudes: Question 5 : le sujet imprime « Take g as 10 m s^-2 » ; cette valeur est utilisée. Le plan d'arrivée est supposé horizontal au niveau de O (portée et durée de vol calculées jusqu'au retour à la hauteur de O), ce que le sujet sous-entend par « horizontal range ».

questions.enonce_markdown: the distance from $O$, of the particle $1.5$ seconds later,
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Take $O$ as origin, the $x$-axis horizontal in the plane of motion and the $y$-axis vertically upwards; no air resistance, $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (printed), acceleration $(0, -g)$.

**Components of the initial velocity.** $\tan\theta = \dfrac{5}{12}$ gives the right-angled triangle with sides $5, 12, 13$, so $\sin\theta = \dfrac{5}{13}$ and $\cos\theta = \dfrac{12}{13}$:

$$u_x = 52\cos\theta = 48\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}},\qquad u_y = 52\sin\theta = 20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

**Position at $t = 1.5\ \mathrm{s}$:**

$$x = u_xt = 48\times 1.5 = 72\ \mathrm{m}$$

$$y = u_yt - \tfrac12gt^2 = 20(1.5) - 5(1.5)^2 = 30 - 11.25 = 18.75\ \mathrm{m}$$

**Distance from $O$:**

$$d = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \sqrt{72^2 + 18.75^2} = \sqrt{5535.5625} = \tfrac34\sqrt{9841} \approx 74.4\ \mathrm{m}$$

**The particle is about $74.4\ \mathrm{m}$ from $O$** (at the point $(72;\ 18.75)$ m, still rising since $1.5 < 2$).

questions.enonce_markdown: the maximum height attained above the point of projection,
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $\sin\theta = \dfrac{5}{13}$ we have $u_y = 20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ (see part (a)). At the highest point the vertical velocity is zero: $0 = u_y^2 - 2gH$, so

$$H = \frac{u_y^2}{2g} = \frac{20^2}{2\times 10} = 20\ \mathrm{m}$$

**The maximum height above the point of projection is $20\ \mathrm{m}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: the time taken to attain the maximum height,
questions.corrige_markdown:
At the highest point $v_y = u_y - gt = 0$, so

$$t = \frac{u_y}{g} = \frac{20}{10} = 2\ \mathrm{s}$$

**The time taken to reach the maximum height is $2\ \mathrm{s}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: the horizontal range and the total time of flight.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The particle returns to the level of $O$ when $y = 0$: $20T - 5T^2 = 0$, so $T = 0$ (projection) or $T = 4\ \mathrm{s}$. This is twice the time to the highest point found in (c), as expected from the symmetry of the path.

**Total time of flight $= 4\ \mathrm{s}$.**

The horizontal velocity stays constant at $48\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, so

$$R = u_xT = 48\times 4 = 192\ \mathrm{m}$$

**Check** with the formula $R = \dfrac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g} = \dfrac{52^2\times 2\times\frac{5}{13}\times\frac{12}{13}}{10} = \dfrac{2704\times\frac{120}{169}}{10} = 192\ \mathrm{m}$.

**Horizontal range $= 192\ \mathrm{m}$; total time of flight $= 4\ \mathrm{s}$.**
